correctness.rationale: For the SPD inverse-Hessian Gram G with offdiagonal signs (+,+,-) and 0<c<=d<1, 2c²+d<1, exact minimization of the two retained coordinates leaves a rank-one H-energy residual. Its worst conditional expected retention is lambda_max(sum p_j v_jv_j^T)=lambda_max(P^{1/2}GP^{1/2}). Symmetrizing leaf probabilities is valid by convexity. For (a,b,b), antisymmetric mode T(a)=(1-a)(1+d)/2 decreases and the larger symmetric mode L(a) crosses it once at a*=d(1+d)/(2c²+d²+3d); L is increasing after crossing on this domain, establishing the global minimum. Cofactor identity makes determinant-volume sampling uniform; eigenvalue comparison gives retention (1+d)/3, strict gap for c<d and 4/3 sharp supremum. Independent numerical simplex optimization at four SPD (c,d) examples agrees with exact probabilities and eigenvalues; finite tests only corroborate the all-real proof.

value.rationale: Optimal sampling of exact large coordinate blocks is a natural E-spectral minimax question. The frustrated negative sign-cycle prevents the usual nonnegative Gram Perron optimization, so a sharp closed-form optimizer and strict determinant-volume gap in a full nontrivial two-parameter cone are mathematically motivated and useful, even though only one step and three coordinates are treated.

limitations: The proof assumes 0<c<=d<1, 2c²+d<1; it does not classify other SPD frustrated G, adaptive laws or nonquadratic updates.
Related all-but-one block theory is credited; only the negative-sign-cycle exact classification is assessed as new.
